reason:
The finding stands in part. I read the code and did not run it in a browser.

Part (a) is a regression on this branch.
- In /Users/rufus/lumen-next/apps/web/src/pages/session/parts.tsx, lines 354-390, the form has one text input. While `running` is true, its only buttons are type="button" (Attach, Stop).
- The HTML implicit-submission rule then applies. A form with no submit button and one field that blocks implicit submission submits on Enter. A disabled default submit button blocks Enter, and main had that button (Send, `disabled={disabled}`).
- `submit()` reads neither `disabled` nor `running`, and the input is never disabled.
- Session.tsx line 233 sets `disabled` to `state.stream !== 'open' || auth.status !== 'ready'`.
- Scenario: the socket is closed or reconnecting during a run. Enter calls onSay. `Stream.send` in apps/web/src/core/api.ts line 244 drops the command without a message, because readyState is not OPEN. `form.reset()` then erases the text.
- parts.test.tsx asserts only which button renders.

Part (b) is not new on this branch.
- On origin/main, Send was enabled during a run. `disabled` depended only on the stream and auth, so a click sent session.say in the middle of a run.
- `Kernel.say()` (kernel.ts lines 98-102) never checked the root's status, and this branch does not change it. The two concurrent runs on one root exist on main too.
- The Composer docstring says steering a running task arrives with the steering slice, so the agent loop belongs to another owner.
- The remaining branch-specific defect in (b) is small. The UI shows only Stop, but Enter still sends.

Severity: should-fix. The text loss needs a run in progress and a closed socket, and the user loses one line of text. No data or money is affected. A small fix is enough: return early in `submit()` when `disabled` or `running` is true, or disable the input.
